title: Adi bin Zayd and the Princess Hind
logline: A poet and a princess fall in love at a glance; a clever attendant who loves him herself brings them together, and after three happy years the king's unexplained anger ends it all in a hermitage in the desert.
moral: A love that began with a passing glance became a long tragedy: happiness at court hangs on a king's mood.
tone: Romance played warm and light for the first two minutes (Mariyah's stage managing, the sleepless night, the nervous proposal), then a sudden, quiet, restrained tragedy. No slapstick after 140 s. Violence and death stay off screen.

beats.summary: Adi, elegant and eloquent, is introduced; then Hind, the king's daughter.
At the place of worship Mariyah recognises Adi.
Mariyah points him out and praises him to Hind.
The glance: Hind looks at Adi and is charmed.
She leaves; a deep mark stays in his heart.
The friend returns: she is Hind, daughter of al-Numan.
The sleepless night.
Mariyah loves Adi too, and hides it.
She pleads his cause with Hind despite her own feelings.
Hind sees Adi from the palace window; her longing grows.
Mariyah tells the king and proposes the marriage.
The king hesitates; Mariyah devises the banquet.
At the banquet Adi asks for Hind's hand.
The king agrees; the wedding follows in three days.
Three happy years at court.
The king turns against Adi.
He orders Adi's death; the tale gives no reason.
Hind leaves the palace and builds a hermitage near al-Hira.
She worships and weeps there until she dies.
A love begun with a passing glance became a long tragedy.

subtitles.ar: تحكي قصة قديمة عن عدي بن زيد، الشاب الأنيق المعروف بحسن الكلام،|وعن هند ابنة الملك النعمان.|التقيا ذات يوم في مكان للعبادة،|وكانت مع الأميرة خادمتها مارية، التي تعرف عديًا من قبل.
subtitles.en: An old tale tells of the eloquent young Adi ibn Zayd|and Hind, daughter of King al-Numan.|They met at a place of worship|with Hind’s attendant Mariyah.

subtitles.ar: أشارت مارية إلى عدي، وقالت لهند إنه أجمل الشباب الحاضرين.|اقتربت الأميرة ونظرت إليه، فأعجبت بأدبه وهيئته.|تحدثت إليه لحظة قصيرة، ثم غادرت مع مارية، تاركة في قلبه أثرًا عميقًا.
subtitles.en: Mariyah pointed Adi out to Hind, praising his appearance.|The princess approached, admired his manners|and spoke briefly before departing.

subtitles.ar: لم يعرف عدي اسم الفتاة أول الأمر، فأرسل صديقًا يسأل عنها.|عاد الصديق يخبره أنها هند بنت النعمان.|لم يستطع عدي النوم تلك الليلة، فقد ظل يفكر في الأميرة ويتمنى رؤيتها مرة أخرى.
subtitles.en: Adi sent a friend to learn her identity.|Hearing that she was the princess,|he spent a sleepless night longing to see her again.

subtitles.ar: كانت مارية تحب عديًا هي أيضًا، فذهبت إليه وعرضت مساعدته في الوصول إلى هند.|وفي الرواية علاقة خاصة بين مارية وعدي،|ثم أخذت تتوسط له عند الأميرة رغم مشاعرها نحوه.
subtitles.en: Mariyah also loved Adi.|She sought him out, became privately involved with him,|and nevertheless agreed to help him approach Hind.

subtitles.ar: رتبت مارية لقاء يستطيع فيه عدي الوقوف قريبًا من القصر لتراه هند من النافذة.|لما رأته الأميرة اشتد شوقها،|فأخبرت مارية أباها الملك بحب ابنته، واقترحت أن يزوجهما.
subtitles.en: Mariyah arranged for Hind to see Adi from the palace.|When Hind’s longing became overwhelming,|Mariyah told her father and proposed marriage.

subtitles.ar: تردد النعمان في إعلان الموضوع مباشرة،|فدبرت مارية دعوة إلى وليمة عند عدي.|حضر الملك مع رجاله، وفي أثناء المجلس طلب عدي يد هند.|وافق النعمان، وتم الزواج بعد ثلاثة أيام.
subtitles.en: The king hesitated to raise the subject openly.|Mariyah arranged a banquet at Adi’s house,|where Adi asked for Hind’s hand;|the king agreed, and they married three days later.

subtitles.ar: عاش الزوجان ثلاثة أعوام في قصر النعمان، وكانت أيامهما سعيدة في بداية الزواج.|لكن الرواية لا تنتهي هنا؛ فقد غضب الملك من عدي بعد تلك السنوات،|وأمر بقتله دون أن تشرح الحكاية سبب غضبه.
subtitles.en: The couple lived happily at court for three years.|But the tale does not end there: the king later grew angry with Adi|and had him killed, without explaining why.

subtitles.ar: حزنت هند حزنًا شديدًا على زوجها،|وتركت القصر وبنت مكانًا منعزلًا قرب مدينة الحيرة.|بقيت فيه تتعبد وتبكي عديًا حتى ماتت.|وهكذا تحول الحب الذي بدأ بنظرة عابرة إلى مأساة طويلة.
subtitles.en: Hind mourned deeply,|left the palace, and withdrew to a hermitage near al-Hira.|She remained there grieving for Adi|until her death.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the English translation is a condensed version of the Arabic in most paragraphs (P1 omits that Mariyah already knew Adi, P2 the deep mark left in his heart, P3 that he did not know her name at first, P7 the happy early days, and P8 the whole closing sentence about a passing glance turning into a long tragedy); both are kept verbatim, so in P8 the English chunk 'until her death.' stays on screen under the Arabic moral sentence.
The place of worship (a church in the classical account) is drawn as a plain domed prayer house with no religious symbol, and Hind's hermitage as a small copy of it; default kept neutral.

The 'private relationship' between Mariyah and Adi (P4) is staged chastely: the two sit talking on cushions with her small heart between them and no physical contact; default is this discreet version.
Adi's killing (P7) is entirely off screen: unarmed guards lead him out and the door closes, followed by an invented WHY? lettering for 'without explaining why'; default is no weapon and no body.
Hind's death (P8) is shown by her empty place, the window light going out and a white dove rising; default is no body shown.
Hind is shown growing old during the hermitage time-lapse, and a YEARS 1-2-3 counter and a 3 DAYS LATER card are added as visual aids; default is to keep them.
The ending adds a symbolic picture not in the script (a replay of the first glance in a round inset and a heart that cracks on the word for tragedy); default is to keep it.
Mariyah is given a visible hidden-love motif (a small heart she tucks into her sash, a brief sad look at the banquet) to make 'despite her feelings' readable; default is to keep it.
implementation_notes: Film length is exactly 180.0 s: duration 177.5 + end_hold 2.5. Set DUR = 180.0 explicitly (the template's last word + 2.9 would overrun the three-minute limit).
All cue times are word starts from planning/inputs/timeline.md; use w(p, n) from timing.json in code and check them against the times written in this plan.
Set LIFE.t = t every frame so all figures blink; suppress blinks (noBlink) in the held looks at 31.9-32.7, 98.1-99.3 and 151.5-152.3.

Three colours carry identity at phone size: Adi green, Mariyah red with a yellow scarf, Hind blue and white with a crown (dark after 157.9), the king red with a crown and cape. Keep these fixed in thought clouds, balloons, medallions and insets.

The person figure is front-facing: 'walking off right' is walk() with the figure translated; 'turning his back' (150.96) is a turnFlip style squeeze and then the figure drawn with no face (draw the headwear and a skin disc over the face, or the cape over the body).

Sets: shrineYard S1-S5; adiHouse (palaceHall merchant) S6-S8 and S13; palaceStreet (marketStreet) S9-S10; palaceHall S11-S12 and S14-S17; hermitageRoad (desertRoad + prayerHouse) S18-S20. Bake each once per option set; live parts are doors, shutters, lamps, u.
The one LATER card is at 127.5 ('3 DAYS LATER'), with the camera and set cut hidden at its covered midpoint. The other time jumps use the window sky (S6 to S7), a cross-fade (77.24) and the counters.

Only four sound effects, all in real gaps: pop 25.45 (the whisper), chime 46.5 (heart settles), whoosh 68.0 (dawn wipe), chime 177.45 (THE END). The narration has no other pause of 0.3 s or more, so the door at 150.04 and the heart crack at 175.58 are silent and carried by a 2 unit panel-only shake.

Setup and payoff poses: Adi's bow (tip 0.14, hand on chest) at 35.12 returns at 99.32, in Hind's memory at 167.36 and in the final inset at 173.5; write it once as a pose function. Mariyah's hand over her sash (70.78) returns at 86.04 and 126.64.
S20 replays S3: structure the S3 pose functions as functions of a local clock so the inset can call them at half speed.
Keep faces and key action above world y 1000; lettering never over a face; at most 12 lettering items in the film as planned.
Subtitle chunks are given in subtitles (4, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 3, 4 chunks); copy them into chunks_ar.txt and chunks_en.txt.

S16 packs twelve actions into 13.6 s around very short words; if it feels rushed, drop the Adi half-step at 147.26 first, never the closed door or the WHY? hold.
The English subtitles are shorter than the Arabic, so some English chunks stay on screen a long time (notably P8).
